Jensen Huang Back In Charge Of Nvidia

Timothy Prickett Morgan

Timothy Prickett
Morgan

Co-Editor, Co-Founder, The Next Platform

Published
mon 23 Nov 2026 // 14:56 UTC

Alright everybody, let’s get back to work.Just before Wall Street opened up for trading, Rene Hass, who formerly ran Nvidia’s datacenter business long before the GenAI boom exploded on the scene and who was reportedly the top contender to take on the chief executive officer of Nvidia, announced that he had extended his contract as CEO of chip designer and now chip maker Arm Holdings out to 2033.

NEXTPLATFORM AD

About a half hour later, Nvidia put out an 8-K filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission that reinstated Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang as president, chief executive officer, and board member, roles that he resigned from – but importantly was not fired from – back on November 12 after several scandals came to light.The 8-K was sparsely worded: “On November 22, 2026, the board of directors of Nvidia Corporation reinstated Jen-Hsun Huang as Nvidia’s president, chief executive officer and member of the board of directors, effective immediately. Following the reinstatement of Mr. Huang, Ms. Kress will continue to serve as Nvidia’s executive vice president and chief financial officer.”A few minutes later, Nvidia’s investor relations organization put out a more detailed statement, which reversed the statement that chairman of the board Harvey Jones, which has been a board member of Nvidia since soon after it was founded in April 1993, made in his new role as chairman, saying at the beginning of the call to go over Nvidia’s third quarter of fiscal 2027 financial results on November 18 that the “Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO” and was engaged in an executive search to find a new CEO to run the company.President Trump, who has been buddies with Huang for the past several years as he mulls over the AI future, has been quite vocal in recent days that Huang should be reinstated at Nvidia, and the statement put out by the board (but not part of the 8-K filing) admitted that this was part of its thinking. “In the process of reaching its decision, the board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk,” the statement reads.

NEXTPLATFORM AD

The fact that Huang resigned from his posts rather then being fired from these posts by the board is very important, because it meant that the door was still open for his return. The board was still trying to figure out what happened, and indeed, the special committee formed of independent directors that is looking at Huang being a target of a “foreign intelligence effort” on the part of China is still ongoing. Moreover, in the wake of Huang’s departure two weeks ago, the board also formed a national security and export control committee, also comprised of independent directors, “to oversee trade compliance and national security risks.” Both investigations are continuing and Huang is fully supporting them and cooperating with them.Huang also spoke in the investor presentation:“I am honored to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” he said. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the Nvidia board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading Nvidia during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”
